scope: Read-only audit of two completed 58-second passes and one completed 300-second pass. No model load, inference, runtime rerun, or source/test/input/report edit was performed by this audit. Only audit.json and audit.md are created.

method.normalization: NFKC, lowercase, curly apostrophe to ASCII apostrophe; original HAN and ENGLISH_WORD regexes from common.py.
method.alignment: Unit-cost Levenshtein traceback; deterministic tie priority match, substitution, insertion, deletion. All repeated occurrences retained. Ordered mixed sequence is additional audit evidence only.

fixture_provenance.generator_behavior: The pinned _synthesize_cycle invokes Apple say with each segment voice, fails on nonzero command exit, and mixes the separate synthesized files. expand_segments removes the voice field from the reference JSON. The recipe and output hash chain therefore support two configured synthetic voices; role names alone would not.
boundaries: No separate auditory or acoustic speaker-identity analysis was performed.
The fixture contains two configured TTS voices, not verified distinct human speakers.
Scheduled segment overlap is not verified acoustic overlap; the generator may produce speech shorter than its allotted slot.
No natural-meeting, low-volume, or general diarization-quality inference is established.
fixture_provenance.speaker_conclusion: The raw model output has one ID despite the two configured synthetic voices in this frozen recipe. The parser retains all raw speaker labels. This run does not demonstrate separation of these configured voices; no DER can be computed from arrival-only labels and scheduled reference slots.

annotation_policy.primary_score: The original benchmark text and scores are unchanged.
annotation_policy.sensitivity_rule: Remove only the exact case-sensitive string [Silence], then call the unchanged original scorer. Retain input→output substitutions and all remaining text.
annotation_policy.specific_annotation_status: Observed generated annotation-like text. Its spelling was not found as a defined control token or annotation in the inspected pinned official documentation/code and tokenizer metadata.

primary_evidence.official_display_behavior: The pinned display adapter collapses consecutive repeated instances of a generic bracket tag when merging cards; it does not remove all bracket tags. Its silence comment describes empty chunks. The paper Appendix A describes no-speech chunks as empty text. These observations do not define [Silence] removal as an official evaluation rule.

annotation_policy.inference: The sensitivity calculation separates annotation-like insertions from lexical substitutions; it is secondary and is not substituted for official CER/WER or first-text timing.

publication_timing.timing_note: The original first_text_ms and journal event use adjacent clock samples. The derived event is not a replacement metric; no per-token or acoustic word timestamp is available.

no_lexical_omissions_in_observed_output.method: Levenshtein over a single ordered sequence of Han characters and English words, then each label-delimited text segment in reference order. This preserves cross-language order and repeated occurrences; it is an audit, not an acoustic metric.

reference_repetition.interpretation: Sustained-run and repeated-context evidence only; it is not five times as many independent lexical examples. No short/long denominator pooling.

maximum_source_lateness_audit.interpretation: The next audio-release deadline occurred while step 31 was still executing. Its completion was followed by about 100 ms before the next release event. The recorded spans establish this overrun sequence, not the cause of the slower encode/decode work.
maximum_source_lateness_audit.phase_scope: encoding includes window preparation/resampling and encode_speech; decoding includes native generation, parsing, and publication. These are wall-clock spans, not isolated GPU/CPU kernels.
maximum_source_lateness_audit.source_lateness_scope: Finite real-time-paced WAV release delay. This is not an observed production capture-queue overflow.
